                                                                                         10/28/2026
                           UNITED STA TES DISTRICT COURT
                        FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
                                ALEXANDRIA DIVISION


 MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,

                Plaintiff,

                V.                                            Case No. 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF
                                                              The Honorable Judge
                                                              Rossie D. Alston Jr.


 KA TIE HALL, individually;
 NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN;
 META PLATFORMS, INC.;
 and JOHN/JANE DOES 1-6,

                Defendants.

      PLAINTIFF'S CONSOLIDATED REPLY IN SUPPORT OF ECF NOS. 90 AND 93


        Plaintiff replies to Meta's opposition, ECF No. 101, to Plaintiffs Rule 72(a) objections to

 ECF No. 84 (ECF Nos. 89, 90, 91) and to Plaintiffs motion for targeted vacatur (ECF Nos. 93,

 94). Plaintiff seeks correction of the challenged rulings and determination of the remaining relief

 on the existing submissions.

 I.     ECF NO. 84 RESTS ON A LEGAL PREMISE RULE 26(d)(l) DOES NOT
        PERMIT.
        ECF No. 84 states that "the Court cannot issue an order concerning Plaintiffs Motions

 because discovery has not officially begun in this case." ECF No. 84 at 1-2. Rule 26( d)(l) bars

 discovery before the Rule 26(f) conference "except ... when authorized by these rules, by

 stipulation, or by court order." Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(d)(l). ECF Nos. 15 and 54 asked for that order.

 ECF No. 84 identifies the absence of ordinary discovery and a Scheduling Order as preventing the

 requested authorization. Rule 26( d)(l) expressly permits authorization by court order. The



                                                  1

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF           Document 102        Filed 10/28/26      Page 2 of 10 PageID#
                                           1042



 objection is to the legal reason the order gives. A court abuses its discretion when it "relies on

 erroneous factual or legal premises." Wall v. Rasnick, 42 F.4th 214, 220 (4th Cir. 2022) (quotation

 omitted).

         Meta answers that the Magistrate Judge "expressly construed Plaintiffs 'Motions as

 requests for expedited discovery."' ECF No. 101 at 4. The label does not resolve the objection.

 The sentence after the label states the premise Plaintiff challenges. Describing the motions as

 requests for early discovery does not change the reason the order gives for declining to authorize

 them.

         Meta also incorporates its arguments from ECF No. 73: that the requests should await the

 dismissal motions and that the answers would not help Plaintiff. ECF No. 101 at 4. Those are

 alternative grounds, and ECF No. 91 at 5-7 answers them. The seven interrogatories ask where

 the two reports originated, what identifying information they contained, and whether they were

 connected to any account Plaintiff held. ECF Nos. 15-1, 54-1. Each permits one of three answers.

 None asks for the reports. NCMEC states that Plaintiff "does not have access to those reports."

 ECF No. 74 at 5. That statement describes the gap: Defendants hold the records and seek dismissal

 with prejudice on the ground that the letters' statements are true. ECF No. 91 at 5-6. Plaintiff

 requests the answers now because Defendants' motions place the content of those records at issue

 before any Scheduling Order will issue. The proposed pleading states its claims without the

 answers. ECF No. 91 at 6-7. Whether to authorize the questions and whether any answer may be

 considered on a Rule 12(b)(6) motion are separate questions. The Court should authorize the

 requests on the existing showing or restore them for determination under Rule 26(d)(l). ECF No.

 90 ,r 16(±)-(g).




                                                 2

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF            Document 102         Filed 10/28/26      Page 3 of 10 PageID#
                                            1043



 II.    META DOES NOT RESOLVE THE PENDING COMPARISON AND DEADLINE
        OBJECTIONS OR ESTABLISH FUTILITY OF THE PROPOSED PLEADING.
        Plaintiff does not dispute the Court's authority to require a comparison document. ECF No.

 91 at 11. Plaintiff produced none through October 7. The objections did not stay ECF No. 64. Id. at

 13-14. The question is whether denial of ECF No. 59, with the filed proposed pleading and the

 existing merits briefing before the Court, was the appropriate consequence. ECF No. 64 issued on

 September 9 and set September 11 as the compliance date. ECF No. 64. Plaintiffs declaration

 states that actual notice of ECF No. 64 arrived at about 9:09 p.m. on September 11. ECF No. 68-

 1 ,r,r 8- 9. On September 13 Plaintiff requested relief from the expired deadline under Rule 6(b )( 1)

 (B) and a compliance period keyed to a ruling on the baseline. ECF No. 67 ,r 7. No comparison

 followed through October 7. ECF No. 84 at 2. NCMEC called the initial missed deadline

 "understandable." ECF No. 74 at 4. ECF No. 84 found "ample opportunity" to comply. ECF No.

 84 at 2. It did not separately address the requested deadline relief or the baseline objection when

 making that finding. Those circumstances bore on whether denial, rather than a defined compliance

 period, was the appropriate response. Meta's opposition does not address them.

        Meta's chronology states that "[r]ather than comply with this order, Plaintiff filed Rule

 72(a) objections." ECF No. 101 at 2. The deadline expired on September 11. The objections were

 submitted on September 13 . ECF No. 67 ,r 5. The weeks of nonproduction that followed are a

 separate period, during which the request for deadline relief remained pending.

        ECF No. 64 required comparison against the original Complaint, ECF No. 1. ECF No. 59

 would replace the First Amended Complaint, ECF No. 5. ECF No. 59 ,r 3. A comparison against

 ECF No. 1 combines changes already made in ECF No. 5 with the changes now proposed. That is

 the basis for the request to reconsider or clarify the baseline. ECF No. 67 ,r 7. Vogel denied

 amendment without prejudice and permitted a renewed motion with clean and marked copies.



                                                   3

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF             Document 102         Filed 10/28/26       Page 4 of 10 PageID#
                                             1044



 Vogel v. RMAC Trust Series 2016-CTT, No. 1:24-cv-2182, ECF No. 37 at 1-2 (E.D. Va. Apr. 11,

 2025).

          Meta states that ECF No. 84 does not expressly preclude another request to amend with a

 comparison. ECF No. 101 at 6. Restoring ECF No. 59 permits determination on the submissions

 already filed: the proposed pleading, ECF No. 59-1; the memorandum, ECF No. 60; and the

 oppositions, ECF Nos. 73, 74, and 83. ECF No. 90 ,-r 16(d)-(e).

          Meta's futility argument rests on ECF No. 83, which adopts the applicable arguments of

 NCMEC and Hall and separately challenges the relevance of Meta's August 13, 2026 filing in the

 376 Action. ECF No. 83 at 1, 3; ECF No. 101 at 5. The proposed pleading pleads the August filing

 as a subsequent fact bearing on Meta's knowledge and state of mind and states that it "is not an

 independent basis for liability." ECF No. 59-1 ,-i 276. Plaintiff does not offer the August filing as

 proof of the April agreement. ECF No. 91 at 22. The inference of agreement rests on the April

 sequence: NCMEC and Meta received the same materials, ,-i 127; each moved against the same

 discovery, ,-i 128; Hall issued two case-specific letters the next day, before formal service and

 before any ruling, ,-i,-i 130-135; the letters served the deterrent purpose alleged, ,-i,-i 174-180; and

 the acts alleged are the issuance and transmission of those letters, ,-i,-i 181-184. Plaintiff asks the

 Court to assess those allegations together under the pleading standard. Section S, ECF No. 59-1 ,-i,-i

 203-215, is separate. It pleads on personal knowledge the account names Plaintiff used, ,-i,-i 204-

 209, and pleads on information and belief what the reports contained and whom they identified,

 ,-i,-i 211-214. Those allegations bear on falsity and on the Hall and NCMEC grounds answered at

 ECF No. 91 at 19-22. They do not themselves establish Meta's participation in an agreement.

 Futility should be assessed against the complete proposed pleading and the grounds already

 briefed.




                                                    4

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF            Document 102        Filed 10/28/26      Page 5 of 10 PageID#
                                            1045



 III.    REASSIGNMENT DOES NOT RESOLVE THE PENDING OBJECTIONS OR
         THE REQUESTED RETROSPECTIVE RELIEF.
         Meta argues that Rule 72(a) review "ensure[s]" that any errors "can be remedied through

 that review, rather than by vacating the orders." ECF No. 101 at 7. Meta identifies review that

 remains to be performed. Plaintiff requests that review and a determination of the remaining

 retrospective relief. Rule 72(a) directs the District Judge to consider timely objections and to

 "modify or set aside any part of the order that is clearly erroneous or is contrary to law." Fed. R.

 Civ. P. 72(a). The objections identify a legal premise (Part I), a finding made without addressing

 a pending request and a baseline objection (Part II), and the choice of denial as the consequence.

 Meta's reliance on available review does not establish what that review will resolve. Plaintiff has

 also requested independent determination of the restored motions. ECF No. 93 ,r 10(R4).

         Meta's authorities involved review already completed. In Brock the Second Circuit

 reviewed the dismissal "anew, without any deference" and had "already concluded that the district

 court did not err"; the second and third Liljeberg factors "weigh in favor of vacatur," and the first

 outweighed them. Brock v. Zuckerberg, No. 21-1796-cv, slip op. at 11-12 (2d Cir. Apr. 27, 2022)

 (summary order). In ExxonMobil "an unconflicted district judge then gave the case a fresh look-

 that is, she reviewed his decision de novo" on "pure questions of law." ExxonMobil Oil Corp. v.

 TIG Ins. Co., 44 F.4th 163, 174 (2d Cir. 2022). That procedure is the independent determination

 Plaintiff requests.

         Meta states that "there has been no finding of any violation of 28 U.S.C. § 455." ECF No.

 101 at 5. ECF No. 96 denied the disqualification motion as moot because "[t]he case has been

 reassigned." ECF No. 96. It did not decide whether Judge Davis held a qualifying interest on the

 dates of ECF Nos. 64 and 84, how any interest was held, whether knowledge existed where the

 statute requires it, or whether an exception applies. The annual reports document past holdings.



                                                  5

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF              Document 102          Filed 10/28/26       Page 6 of 10 PageID#
                                              1046



 They are not a finding of qualifying ownership during the challenged rulings. ECF No. 93 ,-i 5.

 Plaintiff requests those findings to the extent necessary to determine the remaining statutory and

 retrospective relief, on the conditional terms stated in ECF No. 93 ,-i,-i 5 and 10(R2).

         Meta's remaining cases tum on their facts. In Chesher the entities whose stock the judge

 held had been voluntarily dismissed before the challenged rulings, and those rulings neither

 benefited nor bound them. Chesher v. 3M Co., No. 3:15-cv-2123-RMG, ECF No. 330 at 4-6

 (D.S.C. Jan. 6, 2022). Meta remains a party, and ECF No. 84 denied discovery directed to Meta.

 ECF No. 84 at 1. Litovich rejected later appellate review as an adequate answer in the

 circumstances of the documented conflict and the substantive proceedings before it. Litovich v.

 Bank ofAm. Corp., No. 21-2905, slip op. at 19-20 (2d Cir. July 2, 2024). Vacatur under§ 455 is

 neither categorical nor foreclosed; it turns on the risk of injustice to the parties, the risk of injustice

 in other cases, and the risk of undermining public confidence. Liljeberg v. Health Servs.

 Acquisition Corp., 486 U.S. 847, 862-64 (1988).

         Those considerations apply on a short record. ECF No. 84 excluded the proposed pleading

 and denied the specified discovery. Three dismissal motions will otherwise be decided against a

 pleading Plaintiff moved to replace on September 7. ECF No. 94 at 5-6. Later discovery depends

 on the case continuing. If a qualifying conflict is established, the consequences of prior

 participation in those rulings require a determination. The requested procedure preserves every

 existing submission and requires no retrial. ECF No. 93 ,-i 10(R3).

 IV.     RELIEF
         Plaintiff requests that the Court: (1) set aside the challenged rulings in ECF No. 84; (2)

 remove the comparison prerequisite and vacate the September 11, 2026 deadline in ECF No. 64,

 determining the preserved objections in ECF Nos. 66 and 67 together with ECF No. 90; (3) grant

 ECF No. 59, deem ECF No. 59-1 the operative pleading, and authorize ECF Nos. 15 and 54 on the


                                                     6

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF           Document 102       Filed 10/28/26      Page 7 of 10 PageID#
                                           1047



 terms already requested; (4) alternatively, restore ECF Nos. 15, 54, and 59 for independent

 determination on their existing authorized submissions without an additional comparison; (5) if

 the Court sustains a comparison requirement, identify the baseline and set the compliance period

 requested in ECF No. 67 1 7; (6) determine ECF Nos. 66, 67, and 76, including the request

 concerning ECF No. 76-1, on the coordinated basis stated in ECF No.901115-16; (7) determine

 the remaining statutory and retrospective relief under ECF No. 93 1 10 to the extent necessary,

 with any conflict-based vacatur matched to the established period and the particular orders; and

 (8) determine these matters before, or expressly within, any disposition ofECF Nos. 10, 21, or 45

 that would terminate a claim in reliance on the exclusion of ECF No. 59-1 or on the factual

 premises the interrogatories address. Relief independently warranted on the first four objections

 should issue without awaiting resolution of every financial-conflict question. ECF No. 901 16(h).



 Date: October 28, 2026                                                   Respectfully submitted,




                                                                           Marvelle J. Ballentine

 KA TIE HALL, individually;

 and JOHN/JANE DOES 1-6,

                 Defendants.

                                               ORDER


         This matter is before the Court on Plaintiffs Motion for Entry of a Scheduling Order and,

  as Necessary, an Initial Pretrial Conference (ECF _). The Court has considered the Motion, the

  memorandum, and any response and reply.

         It is hereby ORDERED that the Motion is GRANTED as follows.

          1.     A scheduling conference under Fed. R. Civ. P. 16(b)(l)(B) and Local Civil Rule

  16(B) is set for - - - -, 2026, at          , before _ _ _ _ , [in Courtroom_/ by telephone

  or video].

         2.      Under Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(±)(1), 26(±)(4), and Local Civil Rule 26(A)(l), the

  parties shall confer under Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(±) no later than seven days before the conference. The

  parties shall file a written Rule 26(±) report no later than three days before the conference. The

  report may state agreed positions and separately identified positions of each party on each subject




                                                   1

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF              Document 103-1         Filed 10/28/26       Page 2 of 2 PageID#
                                               1059



  in Rule 26(f)(3). Agreement on every subject is not a condition of entry of the scheduling order.

  Oral reporting at the conference is permitted only if the Court, by further order, excuses the written

  report.

            3.    If a Rule 26(f) report is filed before the conference and the Court determines that

  the report is sufficient, the Court may enter the scheduling order on the report and vacate the

  conference.

            4.    The Court shall enter the scheduling order at the conference or within seven days

  after it. The scheduling order shall limit the time to join other parties, amend the pleadings,

  complete discovery, and file motions, Fed. R. Civ. P. 16(b)(3)(A), and shall fix the discovery cut-

  off, the date of the final pretrial conference, and, where practicable, the trial date, Local Civil Rule

  16(B).

            5.    This Order directs conference preparation. It makes no finding concerning any

  party's participation in the Rule 26(f) process to date.

            6.    Nothing in this Order adjudicates the pending objections or applications

  concerning ECF 84 or ECF 96, and no such request is withdrawn by the Motion.

            It is SO ORDERED.

  Alexandria, Virginia
  _ _ _ _ ,2026

                                                                                   Rossie D. Alston, Jr.
                                                                            United States District Judge

                           UNITED STA TES DISTRICT COURT
                        FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
                                ALEXANDRIA DIVISION


 MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,

                Plaintiff,

                V.                                             Case No. 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF
                                                               The Honorable Judge
                                                               Rossie D. Alston Jr.


 KA TIE HALL, individually;
 NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN;
 META PLATFORMS, INC.;
 and JOHN/JANE DOES 1-6,

                Defendants.

      PLAINTIFF'S MOTION FOR ENTRY OF A SCHEDULING ORDER AND, AS
 NECESSARY, AN INITIAL PRETRIAL CONFERENCE UNDER FEDERAL RULE OF
                CIVIL PROCEDURE 16(b) AND LOCAL CIVIL RULE 16(B)


        PlaintiffMarvelle J. Ballentine moves under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 16(b)(l)-(3)

 and Local Civil Rule 16(B) for three forms of relief. First, Plaintiff requests entry of a scheduling

 order after the report or consultation that Rule 16(b)(1) requires. Second, Plaintiff requests an

 initial pretrial conference if one is necessary to obtain that consultation. Third, if either step is

 postponed, Plaintiff requests that the order state the good cause found under Rule 16(b)(2) and the

 date or event on which scheduling will next be addressed. Under Local Civil Rule 7(F), a

 supporting memorandum and a proposed order accompany this Motion.




                                                   1

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF             Document 103        Filed 10/28/26      Page 2 of 7 PageID#
                                             1052



 I.       GROUNDS
          1.    The action is pending. The operative pleading is the First Amended Complaint.

 ECF 5. ECF 84 denied Plaintiffs motion for leave to amend. ECF 84 at 1-2. Applications

 challenging that denial remain pending. The action is not without an operative pleading.

          2.    The events that start the Rule 16(b)(2) period have occurred. Defendant National

 Center for Missing & Exploited Children ("NCMEC") was served on July 31, 2026. ECF 3.

 NCMEC appeared on August 12, 2026, by filing its motion to dismiss. ECF 10.

          3.    The ordinary Rule 16(b)(2) deadline, absent a finding of good cause for delay,

 was October 13, 2026. Sixty days after August 12, 2026 was Sunday, October 11, 2026. Monday,

 October 12, 2026 was Columbus Day. The period ran to Tuesday, October 13, 2026. Fed. R. Civ.

 P. 6(a)(l)(C), 6(a)(6)(A), 16(b)(2). The memorandum shows the computation.

          4.    No scheduling order has been entered. The docket through ECF 101 contains no

 Rule 16(b) scheduling order. ECF 84 stated on October 7, 2026 that "currently there is no

 Scheduling Order in this case." ECF 84 at 1-2.

          5.    The parties' conference under Rule 26(f) is the subject of a separate motion. This

 Motion does not depend on the disposition of that motion, and that motion does not depend on the

 disposition of this one. Rule 16(b)(1 )(B) supplies a route to the scheduling order that does not

 require a completed Rule 26(f) report.

          6.    This Motion does not rest on any Defendant's conduct. Plaintiff seeks a

 scheduling order because the Rule 16(b)(2) period has run and the action is not exempt from Rule

 16(b).

          7.    This Motion does not claim that passage of the scheduling deadline itself

 authorizes service of discovery. It does not claim that the lapse affects the Court's jurisdiction or

 the validity of any order entered since.


                                                  2

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF              Document 103        Filed 10/28/26       Page 3 of 7 PageID#
                                              1053



 II.    SCOPE
         8.     This Motion seeks initial case management. It does not seek enforcement of

 Plaintiffs Rule 26(f) proposals, authorization of particular discovery, sanctions, or reconsideration

 of any prior order. The pending applications challenging the amendment and discovery denials

 and addressing the reassignment remain presented on their own grounds. No request is withdrawn

 by this Motion.

 III.   RELIEF REQUESTED
        9.      Entry of the scheduling order. Plaintiff requests that the Court:

        (a)     set a Rule 16(b) scheduling conference on a date certain within 21 days after entry

 of the order granting this Motion, unless a sufficient Rule 26(f) report filed before that date permits

 entry of the scheduling order without a conference;

        (b)     enter the scheduling order at the conference or within seven days after it, limiting

 the time to join other parties, amend the pleadings, complete discovery, and file motions, Fed. R.

 Civ. P. 16(b)(3)(A), and fixing the discovery cut-off, the final pretrial conference date, and, where

 practicable, the trial date, Local Civil Rule 16(B); and

        (c)     shorten the preparatory intervals under Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(f)(l) and 26(£)(4) and

 Local Civil Rule 26(A)(l), so that the parties confer no later than seven days before the Court's

 conference and file a written Rule 26(f) report no later than three days before it, with oral reporting

 only if the Court excuses the written report. Plaintiff requests that the conference-setting order

 select dates that can be met after the order issues.

         10.    Independent request for an initial conference. If the Court determines that entry of

 the complete scheduling order should await disposition of a pending matter, Plaintiff separately

 requests that the Court determine whether an initial scheduling conference can proceed now to

 establish the remaining case-management steps.



                                                    3

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF            Document 103        Filed 10/28/26      Page 4 of 7 PageID#
                                            1054



        11.     Disposition upon postponement. If the Court postpones either the scheduling

 conference or entry of the scheduling order, Plaintiff requests that the order state the good cause

 found under Rule 16(b)(2) and the date or event on which scheduling will next be addressed.

        12.     This alternative request does not constitute agreement that further postponement

 is warranted and does not withdraw the request for scheduling now.

        13.     The proposed 21-day, seven-day, and three-day periods are requested case-

 management terms. The rules do not impose them.



 Date: October 28, 2026                                                     Respectfully submitted,




                                                                            Marvelle J. Ballentine
                                                                                  Plaintiff, pro se
                                                                 1520 Belle View Blvd, Ste. #5847

                                                                                      10/28/2026
                           UNITED STA TES DISTRICT COURT
                        FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
                                ALEXANDRIA DIVISION


 MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,

                Plaintiff,

                V.                                            Case No. 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF
                                                              The Honorable Judge
                                                              Rossie D. Alston Jr.


 KA TIE HALL, individually;
 NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN;
 META PLATFORMS, INC.;
 and JOHN/JANE DOES 1-6,

                Defendants.

      MEMORANDUM IN SUPPORT OF PLAINTIFF'S MOTION FOR ENTRY OF A
         SCHEDULING ORDER AND, AS NECESSARY, AN INITIAL PRETRIAL
                                         CONFERENCE


 I.     INTRODUCTION
        This action has an operative complaint, appearing Defendants, and pending motions. ECF

 5, 10, 21 , 45 . It has no Rule 16(b) scheduling order. NCMEC was served on July 31, 2026, and

 appeared on August 12, 2026. ECF 3, 10. Under Fed. R. Civ. P. 16(b)(2) and 6(a), the ordinary

 deadline for the scheduling order, absent a finding of good cause for delay, was October 13, 2026.

 ECF 84 confirmed on October 7, 2026 that no scheduling order existed. ECF 84 at 1-2.

        Plaintiff requests three things. First, entry of the scheduling order after the report or

 consultation Rule 16(b)(1) requires. Second, an initial scheduling conference where necessary to

 obtain that consultation, even if the Court is not prepared to enter the complete schedule at once.

 Third, if either step is postponed, an order stating the good cause found under Rule 16(b)(2) and



                                                  1

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF             Document 104        Filed 10/28/26      Page 2 of 10 PageID#
                                             1061



 the date or event on which scheduling will next be addressed. The third request is not a substitute

 for the first two and is not consent to postponement.

        This Motion does not seek authorization of particular discovery, adjudication of any

 discovery dispute, or reconsideration of any ruling. It asks the Court to establish the timetable for

 a pending action.

 II.    PROCEDURAL FACTS
  Date                              Event                            Record
  July 30, 2026                     Action commenced.                ECF 1
  July 31, 2026                     NCMEC served.                    ECF 3
  August 6, 2026                    First Amended Complaint          ECF 5
                                    filed.
  August 12, 2026                   NCMEC appeared by filing         ECF 10
                                    its motion to dismiss.
  October 7, 2026                   ECF 84 denied the two Rule       ECF 84 at 1-2
                                    26(d)(l) motions and the
                                    motion for leave to amend,
                                    and stated that no scheduling
                                    order exists.
  October 22, 2026                  ECF 96 denied ECF 86 as          ECF 96
                                    moot.
  Through ECF 101                   No Rule 16(b) scheduling         Docket
                                    order appears on the docket.


        Three motions to dismiss are pending. ECF 10, 21, 45. Plaintiffs objections and

 applications concerning ECF 84 and ECF 96 remain pending. ECF 89, 90, 93, 97-99. None of

 those filings is the subject of this Motion.

 III.   RULE 16(b) GOVERNS THIS ACTION, AND ITS ORDINARY DEADLINE RAN
         ON OCTOBER 13, 2026.
        A.       The action is not exempt.
        Rule 16(b)(1) applies "[ e]xcept in categories of actions exempted by local rule." Fed. R.

 Civ. P. 16(b)(l). Local Civil Rule 16(A) exempts "[p]roceedings upon a defendant's default and

 matters involving habeas corpus petitions, other pro se prisoner petitions, bankruptcy proceedings,




                                                   2

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF            Document 104        Filed 10/28/26      Page 3 of 10 PageID#
                                            1062



 condemnation cases, forfeitures, and reviews from administrative agencies." E.D. Va. L. Civ. R.

 16(A). This is a civil action by a non-prisoner asserting claims under 42 U.S.C. § 1985(2) and

 Virginia law. ECF 5. It is in none of the exempt categories. Local Civil Rule 16(B) therefore

 applies: "In all other civil actions, as promptly as possible after a complaint or notice of removal

 has been filed, the Court shall schedule an initial pretrial conference to be conducted in accordance

 with Fed. R. Civ. P. 16(b)." Local Civil Rule 16(B).

        B.      The computation.
        Rule 16(b)(2) provides that "unless the judge finds good cause for delay, the judge must

 issue it within the earlier of 90 days after any defendant has been served with the complaint or 60

 days after any defendant has appeared." Fed. R. Civ. P. 16(b)(2). Local Civil Rule 16(B) sets the

 same outer bound: "not later than sixty (60) days from first appearance or ninety (90) days after

 service of the complaint." Local Civil Rule 16(B).

  Trigger                          Computation                       Result
  First appearance: August 12,     Day 60 is Sunday, October         Tuesday, October 13, 2026
  2026 (ECF 10)                    11 , 2026. Monday, October
                                   12, 2026 is Columbus Day, a
                                   legal holiday. Fed. R. Civ. P.
                                   6(a)(l)(C), 6(a)(6)(A). The
                                   period runs to the next day
                                   that is not a weekend or
                                   holiday.
  Service: July 31 , 2026 (ECF     Day 90 is Thursday, October       October 29, 2026
  3)                               29, 2026.
  Rule 16(b)(2) selects "the       The appearance-based date         October 13, 2026
  earlier"                         controls.


        Rule 6(a) governs the computation of "any time period specified in these rules ." Fed. R.

 Civ. P. 6(a). The 90-day interval is not a second period that opens after the 60-day period closes.

 Rule 16(b)(2) selects the earlier of the two. The ordinary Rule 16(b)(2) deadline, absent a finding

 of good cause for delay, was October 13, 2026.



                                                  3

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF            Document 104         Filed 10/28/26      Page 4 of 10 PageID#
                                            1063



        C.      The command and the exception.
        Rule 16(b)(2) states both. The judge "must issue" the scheduling order within the period.

 The judge may issue it later upon finding "good cause for delay." Fed. R. Civ. P. 16(b)(2). Plaintiff

 does not contend that the lapse affects the Court's jurisdiction or the validity of any order entered

 since. Plaintiff does not contend that passage of the deadline itself authorizes service of discovery.

 Plaintiff contends that the period has run and that the rule now calls for one of two things: a

 scheduling order, or a finding of good cause for a defined delay.

 IV.    RULE 16(b)(l) SUPPLIES TWO ROUTES TO THE SCHEDULING ORDER,
        AND EITHER CAN BEGIN NOW.
        Rule 16(b)( 1) provides two means of proceeding: receipt of the parties' Rule 26( f) report

 or consultation with counsel and the unrepresented party at a scheduling conference. Fed. R. Civ.

 P. 16(b)(1 )(A)-(B). Plaintiff requests the conference route if a sufficient report is not available.

 Local Civil Rule 16(B) permits scheduling without a conference where the federal requirements

 are otherwise satisfied; Plaintiff does not invoke it to dispense with both alternatives.

        The parties' Rule 26(f) conference is the subject of a separate motion. Plaintiff does not

 represent here that the conference is complete, and this Motion does not depend on it.

        Where no completed report exists, Rule 16(b)(l)(B) supplies the Court' s own means of

 scheduling. Rule 26(f)(l) ties the parties' conference to the Court's calendar: the parties must

 confer "at least 21 days before a scheduling conference is to be held or a scheduling order is due

 under Rule 16(b)," except "when the court orders otherwise." Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(f)(l). Rule 26(f)

 (4) permits a court, by local rule, to require the parties' conference to occur less than 21 days

 before the scheduling conference, to shorten the reporting interval, and to excuse the written report

 in favor of oral reporting at the Rule 16(b) conference. Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(f)(4). Local Civil Rule

 26(A)(l) adopts those adjustments for this District. Local Civil Rule 26(A)(l)(a)-(b). A



                                                   4

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF             Document 104          Filed 10/28/26       Page 5 of 10 PageID#
                                             1064



 conference-setting order that shortens the intervals supplies dates the parties can meet after the

 order issues. Plaintiff requests that order. Mot. ~ 9(c).

        The 2015 amendment to Rule 16(b)(2) shortened the scheduling timetable to reduce delay

 at the beginning of litigation. The Advisory Committee recognized that some cases require more

 time to prepare a complete schedule, and contemplated that an initial scheduling conference would

 ordinarily occur within the timetable even where final scheduling required additional time. Fed.

 R. Civ. P. 16 advisory committee's note to 2015 amendment. That distinction supports the separate

 request in Motion ~ 10: if the Court determines that the complete scheduling order should await

 another development, the Court can still hold the initial conference now and establish the

 remaining case-management steps. Plaintiff does not contend that the note entitles Plaintiff to the

 particular dates proposed.

        The party-to-party conference under Rule 26(f) and the Court's conference under Rule

 16(b) are distinct events. Plaintiff does not offer the Court's conference as a finding that the parties'

 conference has occurred. Plaintiff does not ask the Court to find that any Defendant has declined

 to participate, to require a written-only conference, or to adopt Plaintiffs proposals by default.

 Plaintiff asks the Court to set the consultation Rule 16(b)(1 )(B) describes and to direct the

 preparatory steps the Court requires.

 V.     ECF 84 IDENTIFIED THE ABSENCE OF A SCHEDULING ORDER; THIS
        MOTION REQUESTS THE PROCESS WHOSE ABSENCE IT IDENTIFIED.
        ECF 84 addressed Plaintiffs motions for limited discovery before the Rule 26(f)

 conference and Plaintiffs motion for leave to amend. ECF 15, 54, 59. It denied the discovery

 motions "as premature" and stated that "discovery officially begins when the District Judge issues

 a Scheduling Order and currently there is no Scheduling Order in this case." ECF 84 at 1-2. ECF




                                                    5

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF             Document 104        Filed 10/28/26      Page 6 of 10 PageID#
                                             1065



 84 did not set a scheduling timetable and did not make a finding of good cause for delay under

 Rule 16(b)(2).

         ECF 84 relied on the absence of a scheduling order in denying the requests before it.

 Plaintiff maintains his objections to that reasoning in the pending review applications. ECF 89, 90,

 93. This Motion presents a different request: establish the scheduling process whose absence the

 order identified. Continued absence of that process leaves no date for the next ordinary case-

 management step.

        If the Court relies on ECF 84 as a reason to defer scheduling itself, Plaintiff requests

 identification of that construction and its basis.

 VI.    PENDING MOTIONS ARE MANAGED THROUGH THE SCHEDULE, NOT
         THROUGH AN UNDEFINED POSTPONEMENT.
        Three motions to dismiss are pending. ECF 10, 21, 45. Rule 16(b)(2) measures the ordinary

 deadline from service or appearance, not from the filing of an answer. Pending motions may be

 relevant to a case-specific finding of good cause for delay, but their existence does not replace that

 determination. The first is a docket fact. The second is a determination Rule 16(b)(2) assigns to

 the judge.

        The First Amended Complaint is the operative pleading. ECF 5. Scheduling proceeds from

 the operative pleading. Rule 16(b)(3)(A) requires the scheduling order to "limit the time to join

 other parties, amend the pleadings, complete discovery, and file motions." Fed. R. Civ. P. 16(b)

 (3)(A). Rule 16(b)(4) permits modification "for good cause and with the judge's consent." Fed. R.

 Civ. P. 16(b)(4). Those provisions allow a schedule to be entered while motions are pending and

 adjusted when rulings issue. The Court retains its authority to sequence the case through the

 schedule it enters.




                                                      6

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF            Document 104          Filed 10/28/26      Page 7 of 10 PageID#
                                            1066



        Plaintiff does not ask the Court to predict the disposition of the pending motions. Plaintiff

 asks the Court to establish the timetable governing this action while those motions remain pending.

 If the Court determines that a pending motion supplies good cause for delay, Rule 16(b)(2)

 accommodates that determination, with the scope and duration of the postponement identified.

 This Motion does not request a stay of the motions to dismiss and does not expand any sequencing

 request already pending.

 VII.   ANY POSTPONEMENT SHOULD STATE ITS BASIS AND THE NEXT
        SCHEDULING STEP.
        Rule 16(b)(2) predicates delay on a finding of good cause. Fed. R. Civ. P. 16(b)(2). If the

 Court postpones the scheduling conference or entry of the scheduling order, Plaintiff requests that

 the order state the good cause found and the date or event on which scheduling will next be

 addressed. A stated basis permits the parties to determine what remains required and when the

 action will proceed. The request for a stated basis is not consent to postponement and does not

 withdraw the request for scheduling now.

 VIII. CONCLUSION
        Plaintiff requests that the Court: ( 1) enter a scheduling order after the report or consultation

 Rule 16(b)( 1) requires, with the preparatory intervals shortened under Rule 26( f)(l ), Rule 26( f)

 (4), and Local Civil Rule 26(A)(l); (2) set an initial scheduling conference on a date certain if the

 Court requires one to accomplish that consultation, or if the Court determines that the complete

 scheduling order should await another development; and (3) if the Court postpones either step,

 state the good cause found under Rule 16(b)(2) and the date or event on which scheduling will

 next be addressed. Plaintiff requests disposition of each request to the extent the preceding request

 is denied or deferred.




                                                   7

                            UNITED ST ATES DISTRICT COURT

  MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,

                 Plaintiff,

                                                                 The Honorable Judge

 KA TIE HALL, individually;
 NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN;
 META PLATFORMS, INC.;
 and JOHN/JANE DOES 1- 6,

                 Defendants.

                                                ORDER


         This matter is before the Court on Plaintiffs Motion for an Order Directing Completion of

  the Rule 26(f) Conference and Submission of a Discovery Plan (ECF _). The Court has

  considered the Motion, the memorandum, the Declaration of Marvelle J. Ballentine with exhibits,

  and any response and reply.

         It is hereby ORDERED that the Motion is GRANTED as follows.

          1.     Participants. Plaintiff and counsel of record for Defendants National Center for

  Missing & Exploited Children, Katie Hall, and Meta Platforms, Inc. shall participate in and

  complete the conference required by Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(f).

         2.      Format. The conference shall proceed by substantive written exchange on each

  subject identified in Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(f)(2)- (3), unless the Court directs otherwise.




                                                    1

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF              Document 105-1         Filed 10/28/26       Page 2 of 3 PageID#
                                               1080



          3.      Completion date. The conference shall be completed no later than 14 days after

  entry of this Order.

         4.       Report date. The parties shall file the written discovery-plan report within 14 days

  after completing the conference and no later than 18 days after entry of this Order, unless the Court

  expressly sets a different reporting deadline.

          5.      Report contents. The report shall state the parties' agreed proposals and each

  party's separately attributed position on each subject in Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(±)(3), including any

  proposed sequencing or phasing of discovery, any requested postponement of discovery and the

  grounds for it, and any proposed protective or scheduling terms. The report shall not portray any

  party's disagreement or silence as assent. A party that declines to address a subject shall be

  identified as having declined.

          6.      Incomplete participation. If the conference remains incomplete, the parties shall

  file a joint status report by the reporting deadline. A party unable to obtain a joint report shall file

  its own report by that deadline. Each report shall identify the participation, exchanges, and

  remaining obstacle. A status report does not constitute completion of the conference, extend the

  completion deadline, or excuse further participation.

          7.      Relationship to other orders. The deadlines in this Order govern unless another

  order of the Court expressly sets different dates for the parties' Rule 26(f) conference or report. If

  the Court sets a scheduling conference under Fed. R. Civ. P. 16(b) by order on Plaintiffs Motion

  for Entry of a Scheduling Order (ECF _) or otherwise, any coordinated conference and reporting

  dates shall be calculated from the date of that scheduling conference as actually set and shall be

  achievable after entry of the order setting them. The pendency of Plaintiffs Motion for Entry of a

  Scheduling Order does not postpone compliance with this Order. The preparatory intervals under




                                                     2

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF            Document 105-1        Filed 10/28/26        Page 3 of 3 PageID#
                                             1081



  Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(f)(l) and 26(f)(4) and Local Civil Rule 26(A)(l) are shortened to the extent

  necessary to meet the dates set by this Order or by any such order.

         8.      Existing matters. Nothing in this Order adjudicates any pending motion, defense,

  or objection, including the pending motions to dismiss (ECF 10, 21, 45) and the pending objections

  and applications concerning ECF 84 and ECF 96, and nothing in this Order modifies any existing

  order except as expressly provided. Participation in the conference does not waive any defense,

  including any asserted immunity, and does not require any party's agreement with any other

  party's proposal.

         It is SO ORDERED.

  Alexandria, Virginia
  _ _ _ _ ,2026

                                                                                William E. Fitzpatrick
                                                                        United States Magistrate Judge

                          UNITED STA TES DISTRICT COURT
                       FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
                               ALEXANDRIA DIVISION


 MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,

               Plaintiff,

               V.                                            Case No. 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF
                                                             The Honorable Judge
                                                             Rossie D. Alston Jr.


 KA TIE HALL, individually;
 NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN;
 META PLATFORMS, INC.;
 and JOHN/JANE DOES 1-6,

               Defendants.

 PLAINTIFF'S MOTION FOR AN ORDER DIRECTING COMPLETION OF THE RULE
             26(0 CONFERENCE AND SUBMISSION OF A DISCOVERY PLAN


        PlaintiffMarvelle J. Ballentine moves under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 26(f)(l)-(3),

 and under the Court's case-management authority under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 16, for

 an order directing the appearing parties to complete the conference Rule 26(f) requires by a date

 certain and to file a written report identifying the parties' agreed proposals and each party's

 separately stated positions on the matters Rule 26(f)(3) requires the discovery plan to address.

 Under Local Civil Rule 7(F), a supporting memorandum, the Declaration ofMarvelle J. Ballentine

 with Exhibits A, B, C-1, and C-2, and a proposed order accompany this Motion.

 I.     GROUNDS
        1.     The action has an operative pleading and appeanng parties. The operative

 pleading is the First Amended Complaint. ECF 5. Defendant National Center for Missing &

 Exploited Children ("NCMEC") appeared on August 12, 2026, ECF 10; Defendant Meta



                                                 1

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF             Document 105        Filed 10/28/26      Page 2 of 9 PageID#
                                             1071



 Platforms, Inc. ("Meta") appeared on August 21, 2026, ECF 21; and Defendant Katie Hall

 appeared on September 2, 2026, ECF 45. Each appearance was by motion to dismiss. Those

 motions remain pending. The Doe Defendants have not been identified or served and are not

 participants in the conference.

        2.      Plaintiff transmitted written Rule 26(f) planning materials on October 16, 2026.

 On that date Plaintiff transmitted by electronic mail to counsel of record for each appearing

 Defendant a written Rule 26(£)(2) proposal directed to that Defendant and a common agenda

 addressed to all appearing parties, and requested each Defendant's written response by October

 30, 2026. Ballentine Deel. 11 3-6; Exs. A, B. The materials stated that transmission, expiration of

 the response date, silence, or refusal would not be treated as completion of the conference. Ex. A

 §§ I, IV, V.

        3.      The October 28, 2026 correspondence presents a disagreement about whether

 planning should proceed while the motions to dismiss are pending. On October 28, 2026, Plaintiff

 wrote to counsel for NCMEC and Hall requesting the position of each of those Defendants on

 three subjects: whether it intended to participate in the Rule 26(f) conference; whether it contended

 that any order or other authority excused or postponed its Rule 26(f) obligations; and whether it

 would oppose an order directing the parties to conduct the conference by a date certain and submit

 a discovery plan identifying unresolved disagreements. Ballentine Deel. 17; Ex. C-1. Plaintiff sent

 a separate email to counsel for Meta on the same date requesting Meta's position on the same

 subjects. Ballentine Deel. 17; Ex. C-2. Counsel for NCMEC and Hall replied the same day that

 counsel considered a Rule 26(f) conference premature because the pending motions, if granted in

 full, would dispose of all claims, because the surviving claims are not yet known, and because

 Plaintiff might seek leave to amend after a dismissal. Ballentine Deel. 1 8; Ex. C-1. The reply




                                                  2

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF              Document 105       Filed 10/28/26      Page 3 of 9 PageID#
                                              1072



 identified no order or other authority postponing the conference, proposed no date, and did not

 state whether NCMEC or Hall would oppose an order setting a conference deadline. Ex. C-1.

 Meta's counsel had not responded as of the execution of the accompanying Declaration. Ballentine

 Deel. ,-r 9.

          4.    The October 30, 2026 response date was requested by Plaintiff. It was not set by

 the Court. It had not passed when this Motion was filed. Plaintiff files now because the October

 28 reply states a position that planning should await the disposition of the motions to dismiss. That

 is a disagreement about timing that a prospective order can resolve. Plaintiff does not contend that

 any Defendant has defaulted on the October 30 date.

          5.    The Rule 26(f) conference has not been completed. Plaintiff has reviewed the

 docket through ECF 101 and has located no order expressly postponing the parties' Rule 26(f)

 conference. Ballentine Deel. ,-r 10.

          6.    A prospective order can resolve the timing dispute while preserving every party's

 substantive positions. The requested order directs participation and reporting. It does not require

 any party to agree with Plaintiffs proposals, and it permits each party to state in the report its

 position on dismissal, immunity, sequencing, phasing, and any requested postponement of

 discovery.

          7.    The requested dates can be coordinated with the separately requested Rule 16

 schedule. Plaintiff's Motion for Entry of a Scheduling Order (ECF _) requests a Rule 16(b)

 scheduling conference within 21 days of the order granting it, with the parties' conference no later

 than seven days before and the report no later than three days before the Court's conference. The

 proposed order here provides that its deadlines govern unless another order expressly sets different

 conference or reporting dates, and that any coordinated dates are calculated from the Rule 16

 II.    SCOPE
        8.      This Motion seeks participation and reporting. It does not request adoption of

 Plaintiffs discovery proposals, answers to interrogatories, production of documents, sanctions, or

 modification of ECF 84. Plaintiffs pending objections and applications concerning ECF 84 and

 ECF 96 remain presented on their own grounds, and no request is withdrawn by this Motion.

        9.      This Motion does not depend on the disposition of Plaintiffs Motion for Entry of

 a Scheduling Order, and that motion does not depend on the disposition of this one.

 III.   LOCAL CIVIL RULE 37(E)
        10.     This Motion seeks prospective case-management directions under Rules 16 and

 26(f). It does not seek an order compelling disclosure or a response to a discovery request.

 Plaintiff's written efforts to obtain participation appear in the Declaration and Exhibits A through

 C-2. No telephone or in-person consultation concerning this request occurred. Plaintiff does not

 represent that the correspondence satisfies Local Civil Rule 37(E). If the Court determines that

 Local Civil Rule 37(E) applies, Plaintiff requests permission to proceed on that correspondence

 despite the absence of live consultation.

 26(f) conference no later than 14 days after entry of the order, by substantive written exchange on

 the subjects identified in Rule 26(±)(2)-(3) and Exhibit A § III, unless the Court directs otherwise;

 completing the conference and no later than 18 days after entry of the order, unless the Court

           (c)   provides that the report shall not portray any party's disagreement or silence as

                           UNITED STA TES DISTRICT COURT
                        FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
                                ALEXANDRIA DIVISION


 MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,

                Plaintiff,

                V.                                             Case No. 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF
                                                               The Honorable Judge
                                                               Rossie D. Alston Jr.


 KA TIE HALL, individually;
 NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN;
 META PLATFORMS, INC.;
 and JOHN/JANE DOES 1-6,

                Defendants.

      MEMORANDUM IN SUPPORT OF PLAINTIFF'S MOTION FOR AN ORDER
  DIRECTING COMPLETION OF THE RULE 26(0 CONFERENCE AND SUBMISSION
                                    OF A DISCOVERY PLAN


 INTRODUCTION
        This action has an operative complaint and three appearing Defendants, each of which has

 moved to dismiss. ECF 5, 10, 21, 45. On October 16, 2026, Plaintiff transmitted written Rule 26(±)

 proposals and a common agenda to counsel for each Defendant and requested responses by

 October 30, 2026. Ballentine Deel. ,i,i 3-6; Exs. A, B. On October 28, 2026, Plaintiff asked counsel

 for NCMEC and Hall to state whether each of those Defendants would participate, whether it relied

 on any order or authority postponing its obligations, and whether it would oppose an order setting

 a conference deadline, and sent a separate request to Meta's counsel concerning Meta. Ballentine

 Deel. ,i 7; Exs. C-1, C-2. Counsel for NCMEC and Hall replied that a conference is premature




                                                  1

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF             Document 106         Filed 10/28/26       Page 2 of 12 PageID#
                                             1083



 while the motions to dismiss are pending. Ballentine Deel. ,-i 8; Ex. C-1. Meta has not responded.

 Ballentine Deel. ,-r 9.

         The parties disagree about whether Rule 26(f) planning should proceed before the motions

 to dismiss are decided. That is a timing question. Plaintiff asks the Court to answer it prospectively:

 set a date for completing the conference, set a date for the report, and let each party state in the

 report whatever position it holds on sequencing, phasing, or postponement of discovery. The

 Motion does not ask the Court to adopt Plaintiffs proposals, to order answers to interrogatories or

 production of documents, to modify ECF 84, or to find that any party has acted in bad faith.

 PROCEDURAL FACTS
  Date                              Event                              Record
  August 6, 2026                    First Amended Complaint            ECF 5
                                    filed.
  August 12, 2026                   NCMEC appears by motion            ECF 10
                                    to dismiss.
  August 21, 2026                   Meta appears by motion to          ECF 21
                                    dismiss.
  September 2, 2026                 Hall appears by motion to          ECF45
                                    dismiss.
  October 7, 2026                   ECF 84 denies two motions          ECF 84 at 1-2

                                    by October 30, 2026.
  October 28, 2026                  Plaintiff requests the             Deel. ,-i 7; Exs. C-1 , C-2

                                    on participation, claimed

                                    conference order.
  October 28, 2026                  Counsel for NCMEC and              Deel. ,-i 8; Ex. C-1
                                    Hall replies that a conference


                                                   2

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF               Document 106       Filed 10/28/26        Page 3 of 12 PageID#
                                               1084



                                    is premature.
  Through ECF 101                   Plaintiff's docket review           Decl. ,-J 10
                                    locates no order expressly
                                    postponing the Rule 26( f)
                                    conference.


 I.     RULE 26(f) ASSIGNS PLANNING RESPONSIBILITIES TO THE APPEARING
        PARTIES.
        Rule 26(±)(1) provides that, except in exempted proceedings or "when the court orders

 otherwise, the parties must confer as soon as practicable-and in any event at least 21 days before

 a scheduling conference is to be held or a scheduling order is due under Rule 16(b)." Fed. R. Civ.

 P. 26(±)(1). This action is not an exempted proceeding under Rule 26(a)(l)(B). Plaintiff has located

 no order of this Court directing otherwise. Ballentine Deel. ,-J 10.

        Rule 26(±)(2) states what the conference is for and who must arrange it. The parties "must

 consider the nature and basis of their claims and defenses and the possibilities for promptly settling

 or resolving the case; make or arrange for the disclosures required by Rule 26(a)(l); discuss any

 issues about preserving discoverable information; and develop a proposed discovery plan." Fed.

 R. Civ. P. 26(±)(2). "The attorneys of record and all unrepresented parties that have appeared in

 the case are jointly responsible for arranging the conference, for attempting in good faith to agree

 on the proposed discovery plan, and for submitting to the court within 14 days after the conference

 a written report outlining the plan." Id. Rule 26(±)(3) lists what the plan must state, including "the

 parties' views and proposals" on the subjects of discovery, "whether discovery should be

 conducted in phases or be limited to or focused on particular issues," the handling of electronically

 stored information, the timing and method for complying with Rule 26(b )(5)(A), changes to

 discovery limits, and any other orders the Court should enter under Rule 26( c) or Rule 16(b) and

 (c). Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(f)(3)(A)-(F).




                                                   3

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF            Document 106         Filed 10/28/26      Page 4 of 12 PageID#
                                            1085



        Those provisions apply to Plaintiff, who has appeared pro se, and to counsel of record for

 NCMEC, Hall, and Meta, each of which has appeared. ECF 10, 21, 45. The obligation is joint.

 Rule 26(f)(2) does not assign to Plaintiff alone the task of arranging the conference, and it does

 not permit an appearing party to decline participation on its own assessment of timing.

        This Motion does not depend on establishing that a particular conference deadline has

 already passed. The Rule 16(b)(2) computation is presented in Plaintiffs companion Motion for

 Entry of a Scheduling Order and is not repeated here. The request here is prospective: a workable

 order setting the dates by which the appearing parties will complete what Rule 26(f) requires.

 II.    PENDING MOTIONS TO DISMISS DO NOT, BY THEMSELVES, EXCUSE
        PARTICIPATION.
        The 1993 Advisory Committee Note expressly addresses pending Rule 12 motions: "The

 obligation to participate in the planning process is imposed on all parties that have appeared in the

 case, including defendants who, because of a pending Rule 12 motion, may not have yet filed an

 answer in the case." Fed. R. Civ. P. 26 advisory committee's note to 1993 amendment (subdivision

 (f)). The same Note contemplates that agreement may not be reached, and that where it is not, the

 report should "indicate the competing proposals of the parties" so that the court can resolve them.

 Id. The rule's text is the principal authority; the Note explains its application to the circumstance

 counsel's reply describes.

        Counsel's October 28 reply states three reasons for postponement: the pending motions, if

 granted in full, would dispose of all claims; the surviving claims are not yet known; and Plaintiff

 might seek leave to amend after a dismissal. Ex. C-1. Each of those is a contingency that the

 planning process is designed to address.

        First, planning can identify how each contingency affects the proposed schedule. Rule 26(f)

 (2) directs the parties to consider "the nature and basis of their claims and defenses" as they stand.



                                                   4

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF            Document 106         Filed 10/28/26     Page 5 of 12 PageID#
                                            1086



 The First Amended Complaint is the operative pleading. ECF 5. The defenses asserted in the

 pending motions are known. A plan developed from that record can state the parties' views on

 what discovery, if any, should precede the Court's rulings.

         Second, Defendants may propose phased discovery, deferral of substantive discovery until

 the motions are decided, or other protective terms. Rule 26(f)(3)(B) requires the plan to state the

 parties' views on "whether discovery should be conducted in phases or be limited to or focused on

 particular issues." Rule 26(f)(3)(F) invites proposals for "any other orders that the court should

 issue under Rule 26( c) or under Rule 16(b) and (c). "A Defendant that believes no discovery should

 proceed until the motions are decided states that position in the report.

        Third, the report places those proposals before the Court for resolution. That is the function

 Rule 26(f)(2) assigns it. The Court then decides sequencing with each party's position stated, rather

 than with one party's position stated in correspondence and the planning step not performed.

        The proposition this Motion rests on is limited: the pendency of the motions to dismiss

 does not, by itself, excuse participation in planning. Plaintiff does not contend that every request

 for postponement lacks merit. This Motion asks the Court to decide when the conference will

 occur. It does not ask the Court to decide any request concerning the sequencing or postponement

 of substantive discovery; those requests belong in the report, where each party states its position

 for the Court's resolution. The Court retains its authority to modify or defer the process under Rule

 26(f)(l) and Rule 16. Nothing in the requested order affects the immunity defenses NCMEC and

 Hall have asserted, which they may preserve in the report and in every other filing. The order

 sought here would require each Defendant to state its position in the form the Rule prescribes, by

 a date the Court sets.




                                                   5

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF            Document 106         Filed 10/28/26      Page 6 of 12 PageID#
                                            1087



 III.   THE CORRESPONDENCE PRESENTS A CURRENT TIMING DISPUTE.
        Plaintiff requested responses by October 30, 2026. Ex. A § IV. That date had not passed

 when this Motion was filed, and Plaintiff does not contend that any Defendant defaulted on it.

 Plaintiff files now because the October 28 reply states a position, not because a deadline expired.

        The reply states that a conference is "premature at this juncture" and that "it seems

 premature to be planning discovery" until the motions are decided and any further amendment is

 known. Ex. C-1. That is a position that planning should await further developments. It identifies

 no order of this Court postponing the conference, proposes no date, and does not answer whether

 NCMEC or Hall would oppose an order setting a deadline. Ex. C-1. The position is stated by

 counsel for NCMEC and Hall. The reply's reference to "Meta and my clients" does not state

 Meta's position, and counsel does not represent Meta. Meta's counsel has not responded to

 Plaintiffs separate request. Ballentine Decl. ~ 9. Plaintiff does not attribute the reply to Meta.

        An order setting a completion date and a report date resolves the dispute the

 correspondence presents. It identifies when participation must occur and how any disagreement

 reaches the Court. No finding of bad faith is necessary to enter it, and Plaintiff does not request

 one.

 IV.    A SUBSTANTIVE WRITTEN EXCHANGE CAN PRODUCE THE REQUIRED
        REPORT.
        Rule 26(±)(2) requires the parties to "confer." The 2000 amendment replaced the earlier

 requirement that the parties "meet." The accompanying Note explains that the parties may confer

 by means other than a face-to-face meeting, while preserving the court's authority to require face-

 to-face attendance by order in a particular case. Fed. R. Civ. P. 26 advisory committee's note to

 2000 amendment (subdivision (f)). The Note does not establish a right to confer by any particular




                                                   6

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF              Document 106         Filed 10/28/26   Page 7 of 12 PageID#
                                              1088



 means, and it does not make an unanswered invitation a completed conference. Plaintiff does not

 contend that it does.

         Plaintiff requests the Court's approval of a defined written process. The October 16

 common agenda identifies the subjects: the nature and basis of claims and defenses and

 possibilities for resolution; initial disclosures and any objections to their timing; preservation;

 subjects, timing, and phasing of discovery; electronically stored information; privilege and work-

 product procedures, including the timing and method for complying with Rule 26(b )(5)(A), which

 Rule 26(f)(3)(D) as amended effective December 1, 2025 requires the plan to address; changes to

 discovery limits; and protective and scheduling orders. Ex. A § III. The agenda keys each subject

 to the provision of Rule 26(f)(2) or (3) that requires it. Id.

         The requested order directs substantive exchange on those subjects and reconciliation of

 positions before the report is filed. It does not request a finding that transmission of the October

 16 materials completed the conference. Plaintiff does not make that contention. The conference

 and the report are separate steps. The conference is completed when each appearing party has

 stated its position on each required subject and the parties have attempted in good faith to agree.

 Substantive disagreement may remain after that exchange; the report records it. Failure to agree

 does not itself establish failure to complete the conference. Ex. A § V.

 V.      THE REQUESTED ORDER COMPLEMENTS THE RULE 16 MOTION.
         Plaintiffs Motion for Entry of a Scheduling Order (ECF _) addresses the Court's

 scheduling process under Rule 16(b): the scheduling conference and entry of the scheduling order.

 This Motion addresses the parties' obligations under Rule 26(f): participation in the planning

 conference and submission of the discovery-plan report. Each motion is independent of the other.

 Mot. ,r 9; ECF _ ,r 5.




                                                     7

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF            Document 106         Filed 10/28/26      Page 8 of 12 PageID#
                                            1089



        ECF 84 addressed two motions under Rule 26( d)(l) for leave to serve limited

 interrogatories before the Rule 26(f) conference, ECF 15 and 54. The order interpreted them as

 "requests for expedited discovery" and denied them as premature because "discovery has not

 officially begun in this case" and "discovery officially begins when the District Judge issues a

 Scheduling Order and currently there is no Scheduling Order in this case." ECF 84 at 1-2. ECF 84

 does not address the parties' conference under Rule 26(f) and does not postpone it. Those motions

 sought particular discovery under one of Rule 26(d)(l)'s exceptions to the ordinary sequence. This

 Motion seeks completion of the planning conference that Rule 26(d)(l) ordinarily places before

 discovery. Plaintiff maintains his objections to ECF 84 in the pending applications, ECF 89, 90,

 93, and does not ask the Court to revisit ECF 84 here. The Motion does not request interrogatory

 answers, production of documents, or modification of ECF 84. An order directing the conference

 would direct the step that Rule 26(f) places before discovery and that supplies the report on which

 the Court may enter a scheduling order under Rule 16(b)(1 )(A); the companion motion separately

 invokes the consultation route under Rule 16(b)(1 )(B).

 VI.    THE REQUESTED DEADLINES PROVIDE A DEFINED NEXT STEP.
        The proposed order sets completion of the conference no later than 14 days after entry and

 filing of the report within 14 days after completion and no later than 18 days after entry, unless the

 Court expressly sets a different reporting deadline. The outer limit allows each Defendant to

 respond to the October 16 proposals, allows one round of reconciliation on remaining issues under

 the agenda's procedure, Ex. A§§ IV-V, and allows the report to be prepared from the positions as

 last stated. The 14-days-after-completion term preserves Rule 26(f)(2)'s ordinary reporting period

 where the conference is completed early.

        The companion motion requests a Rule 16(b) scheduling conference within 21 days of its

 granting order, with the parties' conference no later than seven days before and the report no later


                                                   8

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF            Document 106        Filed 10/28/26      Page 9 of 12 PageID#
                                            1090



 than three days before that conference. The two orders may issue on different dates, and the Rule

 16 conference may be set earlier than day 21. The proposed order therefore provides that its

 deadlines govern unless another order expressly sets different conference or reporting dates; that

 any coordinated dates are calculated from the Rule 16 conference as actually scheduled and remain

 achievable after entry; and that the pendency of the companion motion does not postpone

 compliance. Proposed Order ,-i 7. The parties will not be subject to two calendars, and no deadline

 will run retrospectively.

        Rule 26(£)(4) permits the Court, by local rule, to require the parties' conference to occur

 less than 21 days before the scheduling conference and to shorten the reporting period. Local Civil

 Rule 26(A)(l) adopts those adjustments. Plaintiff requests the shortened intervals to the extent

 necessary.

        If the Court postpones the conference, Plaintiff requests that the order identify the scope of

 the postponement and a definite date or event for renewed consideration. That is a requested case-

 management term. Plaintiff does not contend that a postponement under Rule 26(f)( 1) requires the

 finding that Rule 16(b)(2) requires for delay of the scheduling order.

 VII.   LOCAL CIVIL RULE 37(E).
        This Motion seeks prospective case-management directions under Rules 16 and 26(f). It

 does not seek an order compelling disclosure or a response to a discovery request. Plaintiff's

 written efforts to obtain participation appear in the Declaration and exhibits: the October 16

 transmission of three proposals and a common agenda, Deel. ,-i,-i 3-6, Exs. A, B; the October 28

 requests for each Defendant's position, Deel. ,-i 7, Exs. C-1, C-2; the reply of counsel forNCMEC

 and Hall, Deel. ,-i 8, Ex. C-1; and the absence of a response from Meta's counsel, Deel. ,-i 9. No

 telephone or in-person consultation concerning this request occurred. Plaintiff does not represent

 that the correspondence satisfies Local Civil Rule 37(E). If the Court determines that Local Civil


                                                  9

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF           Document 106         Filed 10/28/26     Page 10 of 12 PageID#
                                            1091



  Rule 37(E) applies, Plaintiff requests permission to proceed on that correspondence despite the

  absence of live consultation.

  CONCLUSION
         Plaintiff requests that the Court enter the accompanying proposed order directing the

  appearing parties to complete the Rule 26(f) conference no later than 14 days after entry; to file

  the written discovery-plan report within 14 days after completing the conference and no later than

  18 days after entry, unless the Court expressly sets a different reporting deadline, stating agreed

  proposals and each party's separately attributed positions; and providing that those deadlines

  govern unless another order expressly sets different conference or reporting dates.

DOCUMENTS TRANSMITTED TODAY
Plaintiff transmits today, to all counsel of record, the following documents: (1) Plaintiff's
Rule 26(f)(2) Written Proposal and Proposed Discovery Plan Directed to Defendant Meta
Platforms, Inc.; (2) the same, Directed to Defendant National Center for Missing & Exploited

1

directed. Each counsel receives all three proposals so that every appearing party can participate
on common matters.
Each proposal states, in its Section I, what the document is and is not: an opening
proposal under Rule 26(f)(1)-(3), not a discovery request, not a certification of completion, and
not a representation that discovery has commenced. Each proposal states, in its Section II, the
procedural posture and the matters Plaintiff preserves, including the pending motions and
applications and the statement in ECF 84 concerning when discovery begins. Nothing in this

1, Marvelle J. Ballentine, declare as follows:
I am the Plaintiff in this action. I proceed pro se. I have personal knowledge of the
facts stated here.
2.
I make this declaration to establish the history of the parties' Rule 26(f) planning
process through the date of execution and to authenticate Exhibits A, B, C-1, and C-2.
On October 16, 2026, I transmitted by electronic mail to Jesse Beringer and
Hillary Dang of Orrick, Herrington & Sutcliffe LLP, counsel for Defendant Meta Platforms, Inc.,
and to Padraic K. Keane of Jordan Coyne LLP, counsel for Defendants National Center for Missing
& Exploited Children and Katie Hall, the following documents: (a) Plaintiff's Rule 26(f)(2)
Written Proposal and Proposed Discovery Plan Directed to Defendant Meta Platforms, Inc.; (b)
1

the same, Directed to Defendant National Center for Missing & Exploited Children; (c) the same,
Directed to Defendant Katie Hall, Individually; and (d) a common agenda titled "Rule 26(f)
Conference by Written Exchange — Common Agenda for All Appearing Parties."
A true and complete copy of the common agenda transmitted on October 16, 2026
is attached as Exhibit A. It is unchanged from the version transmitted. Exhibit A identifies the
three proposals, their recipients, the requested response date, and the distinction between initiation
and completion of the parties' Rule 26(f) conference. Ex. A §§ I, II, IV, V. The three proposals are
available to the Court on request.
Exhibit A and each proposal requested a written response from each Defendant by
October 30, 2026. Ex. A § IV. That date was requested by me. It was not set by the Court. Each
proposal stated in its Section I that it was not a discovery request, not a certification that the Rule
26(f) conference had been completed, and not a representation that discovery had commenced.
Exhibit A stated that non-response, silence, or refusal would not be treated as completion. Ex. A §
IV.
A true and complete copy of the October 16, 2026 transmission email, showing
the date, recipients, and attachment names, is attached as Exhibit B.
On October 28, 2026, I sent electronic mail to Padraic K. Keane, counsel for
NCMEC and Hall, requesting the position of each of those Defendants on three subjects: whether
it intended to participate in the Rule 26(f) conference; whether it contended that any existing order
or other authority excused or postponed its Rule 26(f) obligations, and if so, what authority; and
whether it would oppose an order directing the parties to conduct the Rule 26(f) conference by a
date certain and submit a discovery plan identifying any unresolved disagreements. My email
stated that the October 30, 2026 response date remained unchanged. On the same date I sent a

separate electronic mail to Jesse Beringer and Hillary Dang, counsel for Meta, requesting Meta's
position on the same three subjects and stating the same response date. A true and complete copy
of my email to Mr. Keane, with the reply described in the next paragraph, is attached as Exhibit
C-1. A true and complete copy of my email to Meta's counsel is attached as Exhibit C-2.
On October 28, 2026, I received a reply by electronic mail from Padraic K.
Keane, counsel for NCMEC and Hall. The reply is included in Exhibit C-1. The reply stated that
Mr. Keane believed a Rule 26(f) conference was premature because Meta and his clients have
dispositive motions pending which, if granted in full, would dispose of all claims, because the
surviving claims are not yet known, and because I might seek leave to amend if the matter is
dismissed. The reply did not identify any order or other authority postponing the conference, did
not propose a date, and did not state whether NCMEC or Hall would oppose an order setting a
conference deadline. The reply did not state that it was sent on behalf of Meta.
As of the execution of this declaration, I have received no response from counsel
for Meta to the October 16, 2026 transmission or to my October 28, 2026 email.
10.
As of the execution of this declaration, no further exchange concerning the Rule
26(f) conference has occurred, and the Rule 26(f) conference has not been completed. On October
28, 2026, I reviewed the docket of this action through ECF 101. I located no order expressly
postponing the parties' Rule 26(f) conference.
11.
I remain prepared to complete the Rule 26(f) conference through the written
exchange described in Exhibit A, or through any format the Court directs, and to participate in
preparing the written report Rule 26(f)(2) requires.
I declare under penalty of perjury under the laws of the United States of America that the
foregoing is true and correct. 28 U.S.C. § 1746.
3

Executed on October 28, 2026.
Marvelle J. Ballentine
